newsitem.title: FRANCE: G des Eaux says Cegetel deal to be signed soon.
newsitem.headline: G des Eaux says Cegetel deal to be signed soon.

text.p: Generale des Eaux chairman Jean-Marie Messier said on Thursday the final agreement on establishing the Cegetel telecommunications unit would be signed at the end of April.
The multi-national aims to become the main rival to state-owned France Telecom once the European telecommunications market is liberalised in 1998.
British Telecom will have a 26 percent stake in Cegetel, while Germany's Mannesmann will have a 15 percent direct holding.

Generale itself will have a nine percent direct stake in the unit. It also has a 70 percent stake in the Transtel joint venture with SBC Communications Inc of the U.S.. Transtel will have a 50 percent stake in Cegetel.

Cegetel will own 100 percent of Cofira -- a holding company used at the start of mobile telecommunications in France -- after buying out minority holders TDF and Tractebel . TDF is a unit of France Telecom. Messier gave no financial details.
Cegetel will own 80 percent of SFR, which operates France's second GSM digital mobile telecoms network.
Messier said that Pierre Lescure, chairman of pay-television group Canal Plus , would join the Cegetel board to work on devleloping synergies between telecoms and television.
He also said a deal with France's SNCF rail network concerning a fibre-optic cable network in France would be signed "either Friday evening or Monday morning."
